Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) is a framework that involves several components necessary for creating, administering, distributing, saving, and withdrawing certificates. It requires a significant amount of hardware, software, personnel, policies, and procedures. All these elements are summarized under the term Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) [Source 2].

In PKI, the end user generates a key pair and has the public key signed by a trust center by applying for a certificate from a Registration Authority (RA). The RA is an executive body of a Certification Authority (CA) and is responsible for controlling the identity of the user. Once the information is verified, the certificate is signed by the CA, allowing other users to verify its authenticity. If a certificate needs to be revoked before its expiration, it is placed on a revocation list (CRL) [Source 3].
